[WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p96/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | They swore to cut their fruit in the morning at a late-night or pre-dawn darkness called سدفة.

[JISHUMI:v10p7031/r5] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Ṣarm is cutting, especially harvesting date fruit; ṣarām and jadhādh name the harvest, and the separation between companions is also called ṣarm.

[JISHUMI:v10p7036/r2] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Intending an evil act is itself blameworthy: they were punished for the resolve even before committing the wrong, and actually taking property and denying rights is worse.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p194#2/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | God tested Mecca’s people with drought and hunger, as He tested the owners of the garden.
